subject: Evaluation sprint, acceptance gates, and measurable KPIs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@ledgergrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation sprint, acceptance gates, and measurable KPIs

Hi Ethan — great to connect earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the evaluation plan.

Summary of what LedgerGrid needs (as I heard it):
- Real-time summarization and entity extraction for ingestion pipeline (primary).
- Latency-sensitive responses in UI workflows (sub-second target where possible).
- Tight cost control (forecasting for pilot and 6-month run rate).

Proposed measurable success criteria (suggested, please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 256-token responses measured at Redwood edge for US region.
- Throughput: steady-state 50 requests/sec with 200 concurrent users in the sandbox; peak bursts up to 120 rps for 30s.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.003 across the evaluated prompts (report broken out by prompt type).
- Quality: actionable helpfulness score >= 0.82 on your in-house judgment set (we will run blind evals and share rubric).

Proposed timeline (flexible):
1) Week 0–1: Sandbox prep (dataset ingest, connectivity, security checks).
2) Week 2–4: Evaluation sprint (workload replay + live A/B slice).
3) Week 5: Readout and decision (metrics review + next-step commercial commit).

What we need from LedgerGrid before kickoff:
- Representative sample dataset (~200–500 records) and 5–10 canonical prompts for each workflow.
- Any network/firewall allowlist and proxy details (we'll share the IPs).
- Security contact for SOC2/audit questions and KMS/HSM requirements.

I attached a draft evaluation scope and our network/security checklist to accelerate the prep. If this looks right, I will: (a) turn this into a short mutual action plan doc, (b) schedule a 30-min sandbox prep call next week, and (c) assign owners internally.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eval-scope.xlsx (xlsx), network-security-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Ethan Brooks <ethan@ledgergrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint, acceptance gates, and measurable KPIs

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms is acceptable as a goal, but can you confirm what portion of that is network vs model-inference in your reporting? We'll need the breakouts for our SREs.
- Throughput: 50 rps steady-state makes sense. During our internal smoke tests we see short bursts; the 120 rps ceiling for spikes is fine.
- Cost: procurement will need a tokenized cost report across the three prompt archetypes you saw.
- Quality rubric: I can share a small gold set (approx. 150 examples) and a scoring template — I'll upload to the Drive link below.

Two asks: 
1) Can you include a short note on fallback behavior if the primary model exceeds latency SLOs? (We discussed automated routing to a cheaper variant.)
2) Procurement wants an estimated commercial timeline; we may be able to sign a starter committed plan right after the readout if metrics are met.

I've cc'd Procurement (procure@ledgergrid.com) — they'll review the scope and loop in legal if needed. I'm uploading the sample dataset + scoring template to your Drive link now.

Ethan
Director of Product — LedgerGrid

Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Evaluation sprint, acceptance gates, and measurable KPIs — internal owners and sprint map

Internal — forwarding LedgerGrid thread and assigning owners. High level plan below; please review and confirm you can hit the dates.

Quick owner map (internal):
- Karthik Iyer: overall owner — customer-facing coordination + commercial follow-up.
- Ben Carter: infra lead — sandbox provisioning, dedicated pool sizing, perf run coordination.
- Monica Patel: onboarding & eval scripts — dataset ingest, workload replay, blind scoring, dashboards.

Immediate next actions (this week):
[ ] Ben: create dedicated sandbox pool and share endpoint + allowlist IPs by Tue 12/22.
[ ] Monica: confirm evaluation harness and where to ingest the LedgerGrid sample set by Wed 12/23.
[ ] Karthik: produce mutual action plan doc and proposed 30-min sandbox prep meeting times (I will send invites).

Key acceptance gates for readout (measurable):
- Gate A (Connectivity): sample dataset ingested, IPs and KMS check complete.
- Gate B (Perf): p95 <= 300ms on test harness at 50 rps for sustained 10m window.
- Gate C (Cost): avg token cost <= $0.003 across canonical prompts.
- Gate D (Quality): blind eval helpfulness >= 0.82 and no regression on the gold set.

Notes: for Gate B we will run two 10m steady-state tests and one burst test to validate autoscaling. For Gate D Monica and I will define the blind evaluation rubric before test runs.

Attachments for customer were included in original thread (scope + security checklist) — redwood-eval-scope.xlsx and network-security-checklist.pdf. Also linking the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Please reply with confirmations or any resource gaps.

Thanks,
Karthik

1) Do we expect the 50 rps steady-state to be evenly distributed across 4 model endpoints or concentrated?
2) For the 120 rps burst, should we provision transient burst capacity or rely on autoscaling?

I will start the pool creation today and aim to have IPs and endpoints by Tue 12/22.
